gap: No result ChatGPT got states that to charge a portable power station (Jackery, EcoFlow, BLUETTI, Goal Zero) from a suitcase with a built-in PWM controller, you have to take the controller out of the path and plug the panel straight into the station's own MPPT input. The camping blog author Jesse had to add MC4 connectors between the panel and the Renogy Voyager 20A to do that.
standout_why: I compared the claim against ChatGPT's own answer text. That answer lists 'Portable power station (Jackery, EcoFlow, Bluetti)' as a use case but never says the built-in controller is a problem there. I could not read the 12 cited renogy.com pages (product pages and the RNG-KIT-STCS100D-VOY20 manual PDF) or the outboundpower.com listing. The product pages and the Outbound Power listing returned HTTP 429. The manual PDF downloaded, but its text is compressed and could not be extracted, and the shell commands to extract it were not approved. So I could not confirm that no rival page carries a power-station or bypass note. That is why the score is 2, not 3.
decides: The answer depends on what the shopper is charging. For a bare 12 V battery (AGM or LiFePO4), a suitcase with a built-in controller works as sold: the Renogy 100/200 W N-Type with Voyager 20A PWM, ACOPOWER PLK, or VEVOR. For a power station, the built-in controller is in the way. The station already has an MPPT controller, so the right pick is a plain MC4 foldable panel with no controller. Dealectric lists the Growatt 200 W, ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W, BLUETTI SORA 500, or BLUETTI's own kits (for example the AC180 + 200 W). The page should split the pick on this question.

findings.label: Built-in controller must be bypassed to charge a power station
findings.value: The author had to cut the cable and add MC4 connectors between the panel's junction box and the Voyager controller so the panels could plug straight into a Goal Zero Yeti.
findings.source_title: How To Bypass Solar Charge Controller On Renogy Suitcase (The Camping Nerd)
findings.note: Written by Jesse, published 2022-04-03. Quote: 'you must bypass the solar charge controller since the Yeti already has one built-in.' Jesse says the mod voids the warranty. This is about the older Renogy suitcase, not the current N-Type kit.

findings.label: Factory bypass on newer Renogy suitcases
findings.value: Jesse's update note says 'Renogy has released panels with a built-in bypass' and gives the Renogy 200W with kickstand as the example.
